extracted.intended_audience: individuals, advocates, and organizations submitting public comments on federal rulemakings (Regulations.gov), especially Medicare advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting and submitting persuasive, well-structured public comments on regulations (via Regulations.gov), covering timing, structure, use of templates, content, and strategic tactics. Emphasizes clarity, specificity, supporting evidence, and procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the deadline (time zone specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted by the close of the comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Comment periods close at 11:59 eastern time on the date" specified — ensure you submit before that exact time and account for the eastern time zone.

rubrics_metrics.name: State credentials and expertise up front
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify relevant credentials, background, or organizational expertise near the start of your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with background on your organization or expertise; the CMA emphasizes that commenters should identify relevant credentials and experience to establish credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a single well-supported comment over many form letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and substance in a comment are more influential than volume of form letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization notes that "a single, well-supported comment may carry more weight than a thousand form letters." Focus on unique, evidence-based input rather than mass-produced identical submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize by rule sections with clear headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure your submission so it maps to the rule's sections or specific provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments by rule sections with clear headings to make it easy for reviewers to locate your points and to tie your recommendations to particular parts of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: State your position explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly say whether you support, oppose, or partially support the proposed rule or a specific provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your position explicitly (support or opposition). Examples show effective language like supporting specific proposals while also identifying concerns about implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the proposed rule docket number on the first page
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the docket number prominently so your comment is associated with the correct rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the proposed rule docket number on the first page to ensure the agency can easily match your submission to the correct rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach detailed comments rather than relying on the comment box
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full, detailed comments as attachments when possible instead of entering text only in the web comment box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach detailed comments rather than using the comment box — attachments allow longer, better-structured input and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclude briefly and provide contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: End with a short conclusion and include how the agency can contact you for follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a brief conclusion with contact information so the agency can follow up or clarify points as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about implementation concerns and nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: If you support a proposal, also explain any concerns about how it would be implemented or potential unintended effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioning guidance: use language that supports specific proposals while identifying concerns about implementation details — give concrete examples of problems and possible fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use template comments only as a framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates may help frame issues but should not be copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While original submissions are preferred, templates can help frame issues. The CMA advises against simply copying templates verbatim; instead use them as a starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize templates with stories and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Add real-world examples, beneficiary stories, or professional experiences to make your comment distinctive and persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalize template language by adding "stories and experiences through your work" and beneficiary impact stories; explain unintended consequences with concrete examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate sign-on letters when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple organizations share a position, coordinate a joint (sign-on) letter rather than submitting identical individual templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with other organizations through sign-on letters to show broader organized support while still keeping comments substantive and tailored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus comments on specific proposals or provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need to comment on every element of a proposed rule; target those provisions where you have expertise or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on specific proposals only—you need not address every element. Focus your resources on the most relevant and impactful issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting research and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite studies, data, or other evidence that substantiate your claims and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supporting research and data to bolster your arguments and help the agency assess factual claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request agency clarification where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask the agency to clarify ambiguous language or how it intends to implement a provision when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request agency clarification where needed; specific questions can prompt the agency to address ambiguities in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware comments become public records
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that submissions are part of the public administrative record and may be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that comments become public records — avoid including confidential personal information and be mindful of public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include unintended consequences and beneficiary impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the rule (or its implementation) could affect beneficiaries, including negative or unintended effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include beneficiary impact stories and unintended consequences to illustrate real-world effects and strengthen the agency's understanding of likely outcomes.
